claim: The amended `classifyAcceptanceCriteria` pseudocode pushes the current unit when a **marked fence opens**, but does nothing at fence **close** beyond `fence := false; clear fenceHoldout + fenceTier`. The marked-fence unit therefore stays open after the close marker, and any out-of-fence continuation line (non-blank, non-bullet, non-`Given` — e.g. an `And …` wrap or trailing prose) appends to it. `holdoutRemovalSpans` removes only the `[open..close]` span, so those trailing lines survive in the builder view as a visible unit while the full classification marks them `holdout:true` — exactly the `dodClassify(full)` vs `dodSplit(builder)` desync the spec pins as its third DONE criterion and its second named failure mode.
evidence: §4 pseudocode step 1 ("ELSE (closing): fence := false; clear fenceHoldout + fenceTier" — no `pushCur()`) and step 3 ("otherwise → append to current unit"); contrast `holdoutRemovalSpans` (context file, ~line 376: the removal span ends at the close marker). The spec's own edge case ("Marked fence opening mid-unit … the fence content is its own `holdout:true` unit") and DONE item ("the builder view equals the full set minus the holdout unit") assert the invariant the pseudocode violates.
predicted_consequence: Any spec with a continuation line directly after a ` ```holdout `/` ```integration ` close (no intervening blank line) fails the FAFF-275 coherence selftest the spec itself mandates (`builder-view classification == full minus holdout criteria`), and the builder view shows text the full spec withholds — the builder sees holdout-adjacent criterion content. Fixing it requires a spec-level rule (push the marked unit at fence-close, mirroring `holdoutRemovalSpans`' span end), not a build-time choice.

claim: The spec requires the `dod classify: unterminated fence …` stderr advisory, but its own constraints make every emission site contradictory. §3 pins `classifyAcceptanceCriteria`'s signature as unchanged `(sectionText) -> Array<{text, kind, holdout, tier}>` — a pure unit list with no channel to carry an advisory back to a caller. §4's pseudocode nevertheless places "emit the unterminated-fence advisory" *inside* `classify_acceptance_criteria`, which is also called by `dodSplit` (so a `dod split` run would emit the advisory too — never stated as intended or not) and by every in-memory `dodSelftest` invocation (stderr noise in the selftest the spec says must stay green). The cited precedent ("mirroring the existing `doneAdvisories` stderr convention") is emitted in `dodClassify`, not in the pure parser — so the spec points at two incompatible sites.
evidence: DONE item "An unterminated fence emits the `dod classify: unterminated fence …` stderr advisory…"; §4 pseudocode step "IF fence is still true at end: emit the unterminated-fence advisory"; §3 "keeps its signature `(sectionText: string) -> Array<{text, kind, holdout, tier}>`".
predicted_consequence: A builder must either violate the no-signature-change constraint, emit stderr from a function the file's own comments call pure (double-emitting via `dodSplit` and polluting selftest output), or silently drop the DONE item. Two builders following this spec can ship different observable behaviour (advisory on `dod split` or not) while both passing the DONE check as written.
